subject: Integration guardrails & request/response Qs
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@omnihealth.ai>, Olivia King <olivia@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration guardrails & request/response Qs

Hi Samir / Olivia — great call today, thanks for walking through the use case. Quick written recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the POC: 

Summary of customer's priorities
- Primary: semantic search over medical notes + a reranker for top-k precision (firm wants <5ms additional latency on rerank).
- Secondary: structured tool calling to fetch live patient metadata (SaaS API) and safely redact PHI before passing to models.

Technical items we need clarified (short):
1) Embeddings & storage
   - Target vector dim and preferred DB (they mentioned "existing vector store in Postgres+pgvector") — confirm dimension (512/768/1536) and if they want us to host embeddings or push vectors to their DB.
2) Reranker model footprint
   - Do they need a custom fine-tuned reranker or will a small open model (quantized) suffice?
3) Auth & network
   - API keys vs mTLS vs VPC peering for Redwood Private/Dedicated — which option is required for procurement?
4) Routing & fallbacks
   - Desired SLOs and fallback policy (latency-first -> cheaper model fallback) — confirm priorities.
5) Request/response schema (chat vs completions)
   - For interactive triage (doctors triage flow) we recommend chat messages so you can preserve history and use tool-call structured output. For batch summarization/compliance exports, completions (stateless) are better. Please confirm which endpoints will be used where.
6) Tokenization & budgets
   - Any hard token caps per request? We'll propose default max_tokens=1024 for chat turn + 2048 for batch jobs, but need customer constraints. Also: do they pre-tokenize or expect us to account for multi-byte characters?
7) Streaming semantics
   - Do you want partial streaming for the triage flow (show progressive results in UI) or only final response delivery? Streaming has different ordering/commit semantics for tool calls.

Attachments: I attached an "integration_requirements.xlsx" (placeholder with table of questions) and a simple architecture PNG.

Next steps / asks
- Samir: please answer items 1–7 above so we can draft a minimal mutual action plan.
- We'll propose a 3-week POC: week 1 integration + auth handshake, week 2 embedding indexing + reranker integration, week 3 validation and latency tuning.
- Tentative owner: Ben will put together SDK auth snippets; Marissa will scope Dedicated / Private options.

Thanks — happy to sync if you'd rather walk through these on a short call.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@omnihealth.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia King <olivia@omnihealth.ai>, infra@omnihealth.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration guardrails & request/response Qs

Thanks Aisha — concise, helpful. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions inline: 

1) Embeddings & storage
   - We’re currently using 1536-dim vectors in pgvector (Postgres). We prefer pushing vectors into our DB (customer-managed) rather than Redwood-hosted embedding store for compliance.

2) Reranker model
   - Prefer an open, quantized reranker if accuracy is comparable. If we need a fine-tuned model, we'll evaluate cost trade-offs. Latency target for rerank: <50ms median, <200ms p95.

3) Auth & network
   - Required: VPC peering + support for key rotation. mTLS would be fine as an alternative if VPC is not possible. We need KMS integration for key lifecycle.

4) Routing & fallbacks
   - Latency first for clinician-facing triage (strict). Batch jobs can be cost-first. So prefer routing policy: latency-tiered primary, cost-tiered fallback for batch.

5) Chat vs completions
   - Triage UI will be interactive (chat-style). Summaries/export will be batch completions. We do want structured tool calls for patient lookups — those must be atomic and auditable.

6) Tokenization & budgets
   - Default patient note size is ~8k characters; we will pre-slice notes server-side. Recommend you set conservative max_tokens per API call; initial budget: max_tokens total=1024 for chat responses (we can trim context). Confirm whether Redwood counts tokens pre or post-BPE normalization.

7) Streaming
   - Yes, for the interactive triage we want streaming partial outputs (frontend shows progressive tokens). However tool calls must only be executed once the model indicates the call; ensure no double-execution on reconnects.

Availability: next Tue/Wed morning PST for a short technical sync.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering, OmniHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration guardrails & request/response Qs (internal)

Internal notes / proposed approach before we respond to Samir: 
- Embeddings: support push-to-customer-db workflow. We'll provide SDK snippet to write vectors with provenance metadata. Marissa to own the sample schema for pgvector (1536 dims).
- Reranker: use a quantized cross-encoder baseline (we have a 6B quantized candidate) — run accuracy vs latency perf locally; if they need <50ms median we'll likely use either model sharding or smaller candidate reranker. Ben to estimate GPU footprint.
- Auth & network: Private/Dedicated with VPC peering + KMS is feasible; we need SOC2 + additional paperwork — escalate CS/legal if procurement needs it.
- Tokenization: Redwood counts tokens after BPE normalization (we should include this in the SDK docs). Default suggestion: client-side pre-slice at 2048 tokens for long notes, server will enforce max_tokens per request.
- Streaming + tool-calls: verify idempotency tokens + execution-once semantics. Add a note to SDK: include request_id and toolcall_id; implement at-most-once handling in our tool gateway.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: author SDK auth/sample (api key rotation + mTLS example) by Tue EOD.
- Marissa: build pgvector sample schema + perf estimate for quantized reranker by Wed.
- Aisha: confirm token counting wording with Samir and schedule next tech sync (Samir preferred Tue/Wed morning PST).

I'll draft a short one-pager we can send to the customer with recommended default limits and POC plan.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Samir — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- Embeddings: we will support push-to-customer DB (pgvector, 1536). We'll provide the vector schema and provenance fields (source_id, created_at, embedding_model).
- Reranker: we'll start with a quantized 6B candidate and run perf tests against your latency targets. If needed we can present a smaller model option.
- Auth: VPC peering + KMS key rotation is on the table — I'll loop legal/CS for the SOC2 docs during procurement.
- Tokenization: Redwood token counting is after BPE normalization — we'll include a short note in the SDK. Default max_tokens=1024 for chat responses; we'll add server-side trimming helpers in the SDK snippets.
- Streaming: we'll enable partial streaming for the triage UI and include idempotency semantics so tool calls execute at-most-once. We'll document the reconnect behavior.

Attached: integration_requirements.xlsx (filled with Samir's answers) and a simple POC architecture PNG.

Proposed tech sync: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:30 AM PST — 30 minutes. Please confirm and we'll send calendar invite.

If any of the above is off, flag it now and we'll adjust. Otherwise Ben and Marissa will start the artifacts Ben mentioned.
